findings.title: The model sanitizer does not handle the `[1m]` model suffix shown in the linked issue.
findings.body: The issue shows Claude Code sending `model: "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"`. That string contains a literal `[1m]` (the 1M-context variant marker) and no ESC character. The first regex only matches sequences that start with ESC. The second regex `/\[[0-9;]*m$/` requires the `m` to be the last character, so the closing `]` stops it from matching. The real value therefore passes through unchanged as `claude-opus-4-6[1m]`, and model and pricing lookup for these spans will likely miss. The test only passes because its fixture uses an ESC-prefixed `\u001b[1m`, which is not the shape in the issue. Decide how to treat the `[1m]` suffix: either strip it explicitly (for example `/\[1m\]$/`) or keep it on purpose. Then add a fixture that uses the issue's exact string.

findings.title: Any span carrying a generic `span.type` attribute is now exported as an LLM span.
findings.body: `span.type` is not specific to Claude Code. Datadog-style and other instrumentations set it on ordinary spans (for example `web`, `db`, `http`, `sql`). With this check, the default export predicate returns true for any span that has the key at all. Unrelated HTTP and DB spans that the smart filter used to drop are now sent to Latitude. That adds noise and cost, and it can export data nobody meant to send. Match only the Claude Code values instead, for example `span.type` set to `interaction`, `llm_request`, `tool` and so on, or require `span.type` together with `user_prompt` or `llm_request.context`.
